name: Fisheries Scientist
title: Fisheries Scientist (B.F.Sc)
intro: From Class 12 PCB to a fisheries career: CUET-UG for ICAR's national quota or your state's admission, the 4-year B.F.Sc, an optional M.F.Sc, then state departments, industry, banks or ICAR research via ASRB.

phases.title: Class 12 PCB
phases.summary: Biology is key; some colleges also accept PCM or PCMB.
points: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology is the standard requirement.
Some colleges accept PCM or PCMB.
Minimum marks are set by each university.

phases.title: CUET-UG or state admission
phases.summary: ICAR national-quota seats through CUET-UG, or your state agricultural university's seats.
points: ICAR uses CUET-UG for its undergraduate national quota, followed by ICAR counselling.
State-quota seats follow the state agricultural/fisheries university's admission rules.
Apply through both routes where you can.

phases.title: B.F.Sc (4 years)
phases.summary: Aquaculture, fish biology, processing and economics.
points: B.F.Sc is a 4-year professional degree in agriculture and allied sciences.
Subjects cover aquaculture, fish biology, fish processing and fisheries economics.
Hatcheries, feed companies and processing plants hire freshers.

phases.title: M.F.Sc (optional)
points: An M.F.Sc is reached through ICAR's postgraduate entrance.
It is the usual step towards research and scientist posts.
ICAR scientists are recruited by the Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board (ASRB).

phases.title: Career
phases.summary: State fisheries departments, industry, banks, or research via ASRB.
points: Government: state fisheries departments (fisheries officer posts through state PSCs), ICAR fisheries institutes and export inspection bodies.
Private: aquaculture farms, hatcheries, feed and seafood processing companies, export houses; banks hire agricultural field officers.
Running your own aquaculture farm can be profitable but carries risk.
